messages:
maria: FYI rolling the log-collector egress cutover in eu-west-1 now. Noticed a few GPU nodes stuck in provisioning with KMS decrypt errors after the policy push. Anyone seeing this?
raj: seeing ~6 nodes stuck, init stuck on 'decrypting keys' step. Logs show `kms:Decrypt` failures and 403-ish responses from keystore proxy.
oncall-sre: investigating — control plane shows outbound TCP to collector IPs blocked (RST). Firewall rule applied ~5m ago by release job. NatGW metrics for that subnet dropped to zero for collector ports.
sasha: that was my TF change earlier: `module.log_collector.egress = var.new_collector_allowlist` — I only added hostnames, not the IP ranges. DNS TTL + new collector pool means missing IPs. Patch below:
```hcl
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "egress_collector" {
  type        = "egress"
  from_port   = 443
  to_port     = 443
  protocol    = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks = local.collector_ips // resolved at plan time
}
```
maria: hmm, why would KMS decrypt depend on log collector egress? Shouldn't keystore be independent?
raj: turns out keystore agent does a synchronous audit write on startup (we enable FIPS/audit trace in dedicated fleets). If audit write to collector blocks (sync), the agent waits and fails decrypt until ack. So blocked egress -> keystore startup stalls -> node can't decrypt.
sasha: yep this is a known behaviour from the audit plugin — synchronous by default for stricter compliance.
oncall-sre: quick mitigation options: 1) revert the new allowlist TF change (fast) 2) add collector IP ranges to SG (fast) 3) patch keystore pods to enable `AUDIT_ASYNC=true` so startup doesn't block (medium). Security will want a temporary TTL on async.
maria: which is least blasty?
raj: revert is simplest and minimal changeset. But revert delays migration. Patch to keystore to set async on a small canary might be faster to get nodes passing.
sasha: I can push canary patch to staging in <10m. Will need security signoff for async for prod though.
oncall-sre: can do canary 3 nodes in eu-west-1, then revert TF in parallel. I'll coordinate.
maria: ok do canary + revert. Raj, can you open PR for TF rollback?
raj: on it. PR #8241 created to revert egress allowlist.
deploy-bot: deploy: PR #8241 merged to staging — canary rollout started (maria/raj/sasha oncall).
sasha: canary results: 3/3 canary nodes now pass KMS decrypt and join the pool. Keystore CPU + memory ~2x for the pod while async toggled off, but stable. Observability: logs show successful audit writes queued rather than blocking.
maria: good sign. If canary holds, revert TF then we do a controlled cutover with IP ranges and a fallback CIDR.
oncall-sre: note: temporary revert will re-route logs to legacy collector (cross-az egress). Finance estimate: ~+$2.1k/day if we stay on legacy path for 48h. Marking cost impact.
raj: pinging finance leads after we confirm schedule.
sasha: I'll open follow-up RFC: better rollout plan should include resolved IP ranges, pre-warm DNS, and a non-blocking audit mode during migration. Also add automation to validate collector IP reachability in release checklist.
maria: I'll draft the postmortem/runbook. Action items: revert TF (raj), keystore canary patch (sasha), runbook update (maria), update release checklist (oncall-sre).
oncall-sre: adding runbook item now. I'll also add a monitoring alert to detect keystore startup audit latency > 5s.
maria: thanks. keeping thread pinned for 2h for any followups. :thumbsup:
raj: noted.
sasha: will follow up with RFC link once created. :spiral_note_pad:
deploy-bot: info: scheduled rollback to old egress policy in progress (ETA 15m).
